title: runtime policy compile race causing deny->allow flip for in-flight requests
creator: Amina Patel
description: Summary: We observed production incidents where recent policy updates (deny rules rolled out for an org/route) did not prevent a small fraction of requests — they were allowed after the policy change despite telemetry showing the new rule was active. This ticket captures the ongoing investigation and proposed remediation for a concurrency/race in the runtime policy compilation path that leads to stale compiled evaluators being used for in-flight requests, producing a deny->allow flip.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start runtime with policy evaluator v2 with evaluator-cache enabled
2) Send steady traffic at ~1200 rps for route /v1/chat with per-key and org-level deny rule about 'suspicious-key'
3) Push a policy update that adds a hard deny for the org (via control-plane), triggering policy-compile on nodes
4) Simultaneously cause a small burst of in-flight requests that hit the fast-path evaluator (cached compiled evaluator reference),

5) Observe that a subset of burst requests are served (allowed) even though the compiled policy in control-plane shows deny should have matched; allowed requests correspond to the in-flight window during compilation swap.
investigation_findings: - The runtime keeps a pointer to a compiledPolicy object used by the fast evaluation path to minimize GC and allocations.

- Policy updates compile a new compiledPolicy and swap the pointer under a lightweight mutex, but evaluator fast-path uses an unsynchronized read for performance and assumes eventual pointer consistency.

- Under heavy concurrency the fast-path can read the old pointer while the slow path is performing a multi-step replacement (compile -> populate indexes -> publish). In the window between publish of 'matcher table' and final pointer swap, partially-initialized state led to guards in the evaluation returning 'no-match' and allowing requests to fall through to a permissive fallback.
- The failure surface is amplified when combined with route-level prefix caching (fast-path bypass) and with in-flight requests that already have a cached auth/token context.

- Reproducible in staging with a tight timing harness; flamegraphs show lock contention around policy-compile briefly, and the unsynchronized read is the root cause of stale/mid-constructed object visibility.
logs_evidence: 2026-03-09T14:23:12.347Z DEBUG policy: compile start id=pol-88 org=acme
2026-03-09T14:23:12.541Z INFO policy: matcher index populated id=pol-88 nodes=3
2026-03-09T14:23:12.542Z WARN policy: publish delayed id=pol-88 reason=waiting-for-shard-sync
2026-03-09T14:23:12.543Z DEBUG evaluator: fast-path eval key=s-9 route=/v1/chat result=ALLOW compiled_policy_ptr=0x7ff0
2026-03-09T14:23:12.543Z DEBUG evaluator: fast-path eval key=s-9 route=/v1/chat result=DENY compiled_policy_ptr=0x81f0
root_cause: Race between policy compilation/publish workflow and evaluator fast-path unsynchronized reads of the compiledPolicy pointer. The fast-path allows a permissive fallback when it sees a partially-initialized matcher state, and this window can allow requests that should be denied.
proposed_fix: Make compiledPolicy pointer swap atomic and ensure published compiledPolicy is fully initialized before any fast-path reader can observe it. Concretely: (1) introduce a versioned pointer + memory barrier on publish, (2) remove permissive fast-path fallback — instead block briefly or delegate to a slow-path evaluator that performs safe checks, (3) add a robust in-memory invariant test that validates compiledPolicy completeness after compile and before swap.
additional_mitigation: Temporarily disable fast-path unsynchronized reads for canary nodes, enable compile throttling to reduce concurrent compiles, and apply a control-plane rate-limit for policy rollouts to avoid simultaneous compiles across many nodes.
tests_added: integration: race-harness that concurrently compiles and evaluates with randomized timings
e2e: staging rollout with synthetic traffic spike to validate deny counts increase and allowed-after-deny disappears
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix behind feature-flag. 2) Deploy to runtime-canary subset (5% capacity) and monitor deny_count, allow_count, and error rates for 24h. 3) If stable, increase to 25% over 6h, then full rollout. 4) Backfill telemetry to ensure no historical accounting gaps. 5) Re-enable fast-path incrementally once invariants hold.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add Grafana panels: rate_enforcer:deny_count, rate_enforcer:allow_after_policy_update, runtime:policy-compile-latency; create PagerDuty rule if allow_after_policy_update > 0 for 3 consecutive minutes during rollout.
